Could not build an efficiency curve from the generated response: {1}

How this far-field detector answers off-axis, near-field and uncertainty-aware queries.

  • Flat Disk - the classic far-field model: efficiency is the on-axis curve scaled by solid angle, with an energy-correlated uncertainty you edit on the Anchor tab. No geometry is modeled.
  • Geometry Modeled - a Monte-Carlo response, built from the detector geometry below and grounded to the efficiency points on the Anchor tab, supplies the distance/angle dependence and its own finer uncertainty.

Switching a geometry-modeled detector back to Flat Disk detaches its response on "Use" (you will be asked to confirm).

The detector's measured efficiency points, which the Activity/Shielding fit can fold into its results. Edit each point below - its energy, absolute efficiency, and the statistical and certificate uncertainties on that efficiency. "Stat. %" is independent from one point to the next; "Cert. %" is the source activity uncertainty, and points sharing a source are treated as sharing it. (A Monte-Carlo-characterized response supplies its own, finer, uncertainty and overrides these points.)

The detector's efficiency points and their uncertainties, which the Activity/Shielding fit can fold into its results. For each point, "Stat. %" is the part that is independent from one energy to the next (e.g. Monte-Carlo convergence), and "Corr. %" is the part that moves together across energy (e.g. the ISOCS baseline modeling uncertainty) - how strongly it moves together is set below. Leave "Stat. %" blank to use the default uncertainty.

The efficiency equation exp( A0 + A1*log(x) + A2*log(x)2 + ... ) and the covariance among its coefficients, which the Activity/Shielding fit can fold into its results. The diagonal is the 1-sigma uncertainty of each coefficient (absolute, not a percent - these are logs), and the off-diagonal is the correlation between them. Fitted coefficients are strongly correlated, so the off-diagonal matters as much as the diagonal.

The efficiency formula, with energy as x, and its uncertainty. "Default uncertainty" alone gives one flat fractional uncertainty at every energy; add rows below to give per-energy uncertainties instead, splitting each into the part independent from one energy to the next ("Stat. %") and the part that moves together across energy ("Corr. %"), as an ISOCS .ecc file does.
The full-energy intrinsic efficiency as a function of energy, with energy written as x in the units selected below.
